why_use_this:
Reach for this package when a vāṇी program needs to run inference through a pre-built TensorRT engine on an NVIDIA GPU -- the highest-throughput, lowest-latency way to serve a trained deep-learning model on NVIDIA hardware. This package does NOT build engines from a model (that's TensorRT's own trtexec CLI tool's job, run once offline); it loads an already-built .engine file, inspects its input/output bindings, and runs inference. Pair it with vani-cuda for the device-memory allocation and host<->device copies the bindings array needs.

**Read this before using anything below -- this package carries real, unusual risk beyond the rest of the hardware-acceleration tier**: it was written from TensorRT's documented API contract, but TensorRT itself was never available to check the shim against at all in the development environment (no NVIDIA Developer account access, unlike the CUDA/HIP Toolkits which were at least apt-installable). It also targets one specific generation of TensorRT's API (the classic bindings-based Execution API) that newer TensorRT 10.x releases have partially deprecated. See the README's "Hardware AND API-version verification status" section -- this is not the usual boilerplate caveat, it's a real, acknowledged possibility that this needs porting work before it functions on a current TensorRT install.
